title: Drop the pensioners’ tax allowance
name: Drop the pensioners’ tax allowance
headline: Drop pensioner allowance. Raises £0.1bn in 2029-30.
description: From April 2027 to April 2030 a pensioner whose income is no more than the new state pension pays no income tax on it, with the allowance tapering above that. Switch this on to drop it.

baselinePolicy.text: A pension tax allowance removes income tax for pensioners with total income up to the new state pension from 6 April 2027 until 5 April 2030 (Table 6.1 line 52).

source.quote: The Allowance applies in full where total income is no more than the annual new State Pension, with entitlement tapered as income rises above this threshold.

alreadyIncludes: A pension tax allowance removes income tax for pensioners with total income up to the new state pension from 6 April 2027 until 5 April 2030 (Table 6.1 line 52).

lines.title: Pension Tax Allowance: Remove the income tax liability for pensioners with total income up to the value of the new State Pension from 6 April 2027 until 5 April 2030

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
The allowance ends in April 2030 as announced, so the line turns from a cost to a small yield in 2030-31; dropping it moves those years too.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
